claim: VeRPO converts per-test-case partial success into a dense, theoretically-corrected RL reward for code generation and outperforms outcome-driven and reward-model baselines.
stance_target: novelty of 'dense per-requirement execution reward for code RL' as an open AAAI direction
scope_conditions: critic-free RL for code generation, multiple benchmarks and settings, Jan-May 2026
quoted_support: Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks and settings demonstrate that VeRPO outperforms outcome-driven and RM-based baselines, achieving up to +8.83 pass@1 gain with negligible time cost (< 0.02%) and zero GPU memory overhead.

claim: Naive weighted-sum partial-success rewards for code RL suffer from a 'cardinality bias' that disproportionately favors easy-test gains over frontier-test progress.
stance_target: mechanism of dense per-test reward design for code RL
scope_conditions: weighted-sum partial-success reward formulations in RL for code generation
quoted_support: We analyze partial-success rewards using a weighted sum formulation, theoretically identifying a critical cardinality bias that causes policy updates to disproportionately favor gains from easy-test successes over progress on frontier tests.

claim: VeRPO's density-calibrated local reward is combined with global execution-outcome reward to align local partial-success signal with end-to-end functional correctness.
stance_target: design space for per-test-case dense reward in code RL
scope_conditions: RL framework design for code generation
quoted_support: VeRPO introduces a dynamic, density-calibrated local reward that explicitly corrects this bias and provides robust dense supervision from partial success. To enhance alignment with end-to-end functional correctness, VeRPO further integrates the local dense reward with global execution outcomes.
